newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rubber stable in late trading.

text.p: Indonesian tyre-grade SIR20 offer prices were stable in late trading on Thursday amid sluggish consumer demand, traders said.
"We haven't heard any fresh deals today and consumer demand is weak. If this bearish trend continues, prices may fall again in the coming days," said one trader.

Traders said offer prices were unchanged at 49.25 cents/lb fob Palembang for June shipment after a deal in the morning, at 49.75 fob Medan and Surabaya, at 49.50 fob Padang and at 49.25 fob Pontianak and Jambi.
They said they did not hear of any fresh enquiries.
"The market is desperately in need of foreign support to boost sentiment. There has been sporadic buying, but it has just failed to lift prices," said one trader.
He said prices might fall to as low as 45.00 U.S. cents/lb.
Others said many traders in Medan, North Sumatra, where current wintering has led to tight supply, were adamant they would not sell below 50.00 cents/lb.
But a number of traders in other cities believed the Medan traders lose out. "Buyers can look for rubber in Palembang or Surabaya for instance," said one trader.
Traders said supply was generally ample in Indonesia despite the wintering in Medan.
